{{Infobox integer sequence|name=Hooley's delta function|named_after=[[Christopher Hooley]]|publication_year=1979|author=[[Paul Erdős]]|OEIS=A226898|first_terms=1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1}}{{Short description|Mathematical function}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Hooley's delta function''', also called '''Erdős--Hooley delta-function''', defines the maximum number of divisors of <math> n </math> in <math> [u, eu] </math> for all <math> u </math>, where <math> e </math> is [[Euler's number]]. It is usually denoted <math> \Delta(n) </math>. The first few terms of this sequence are
:<math>1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 2, 1, 4, \dots</math>
{{OEIS|id=A226898}}.

==History==
The sequence was first introduced by [[Paul Erdős]] in 1974,<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.4153/CMB-1974-108-5 |title=On abundant-like numbers |year=1974 |last=Erdös |first=Paul |journal=[[Canadian Mathematical Bulletin]] |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=599–602 |s2cid=124183643 |authorlink=Paul Erdős}}</ref> then studied by [[Christopher Hooley]] in 1979.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Hooley |first=C. |authorlink=Christopher Hooley |title=On a new technique and its applications to the theory of numbers |doi=10.1112/plms/s3-38.1.115 |year=1979 |journal=[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]] |series=3 |volume=38 |pages=115–151}}</ref>

In 2023, [[Dimitris Koukoulopoulos]] and [[Terence Tao]] proved that
:<math>\sum_{k=1}^n \Delta(k) \ll n (\log \log n)^{11/4} </math>
for <math>n \ge 100</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |title=An upper bound on the mean value of the Erdős–Hooley Delta function |year=2023 |last1=Koukoulopoulos |first1=Dimitris |author1-link=Dimitris Koukoulopoulos |last2=Tao |first2=Terence |author2-link=Terence Tao |journal=[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]] |volume=127 |issue=6 |pages=1865–1885 |doi=10.1112/plms.12572 |doi-access=free }}</ref> In particular, the [[Average order of an arithmetic function|average order]] of <math> \Delta(n) </math> to <math> k </math> is <math> O((\log n)^k) </math> for any <math> k > 0 </math>.

In 2024, [[Kevin Ford (mathematician) |Kevin Ford]] along with Koukoulopoulos and Tao proved the lower bound
:<math>\sum_{k=1}^n \Delta(k) \gg n (\log \log n)^{1+\eta-\epsilon},</math>
where <math>\epsilon</math> is fixed, <math>\eta=0.3533227\ldots</math>, and <math>n \geq 100</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |title=A lower bound on the mean value of the Erdős–Hooley Delta function |year=2024 |last1=Ford |first1=Kevin |author1-link=Kevin Ford (mathematician) |last2=Koukoulopoulos |first2=Dimitris |author2-link=Dimitris Koukoulopoulos |last3=Tao |first3=Terence |author3-link=Terence Tao |journal=[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]] |volume=129 |issue=1 |pages= |doi=10.1112/plms.12618|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Usage ==
This function measures the tendency of [[Divisor|divisors]] of a number to cluster.

The growth of this sequence is limited by <math>\Delta(mn) \leq \Delta(n) d(m)</math>, where <math>d(n)</math> is the [[Divisor function|number of divisors]] of <math>n</math>.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greathouse |first=Charles R. |title=Sequence A226898 (Hooley's Delta function: maximum number of divisors of n in [u, eu] for all u. (Here e is Euler's number 2.718... = A001113.)) |url=https://oeis.org/A226898 |access-date=2022-12-18 |website=The [[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]] |publisher=OEIS Foundation}}</ref>
